claims.text: The baseline is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate without TiC nanoparticles.
The controlled modification is the addition of 1 at.% TiC nanoparticles to the coating.
Adding 1 at.% TiC nanoparticles produces a dispersed nanoparticle nanocomposite structure.
TiC nanoparticles reinforce the FeNiCrCoCu coating through load transfer.
TiC nanoparticles constrain plastic deformation during sliding.
At 500°C, 10 N normal load, and 0.1 m/s sliding speed, the TiC-modified coating will have greater wear resistance than the TiC-free baseline.
Under the stated sliding conditions, the TiC-modified coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation than the TiC-free baseline.
The proposed wear and deformation improvements are specifically expected in the 500°C operating regime.
The magnitude of the improvements depends on the uniformity of TiC nanoparticle distribution.
The magnitude of the improvements depends on the coating-processing technique.

contradictions.description: The hypothesized mediator is a dispersion of TiC nanoparticles, but the proposed falsification experiment deliberately uses agglomerated TiC. Failure of an agglomerated coating would not directly falsify a mechanism premised on effective dispersion.
